scope: Catalog-backed optimized-view relations with typed schema and constant-value transport
repairs: Table scans reference exact table objects, with separate catalog schema identity. Java reconstruction supplies CalciteTableDescription rather than placeholder tables.
Column type identities, names and quoting, default and lateness expressions, positions, primary-key and unused flags, and optional positioned properties are retained.
Constant-value uses retain shared expression identity and reject table inputs, correlations and window aggregates; required nullable metadata fields distinguish missing from null.
Uncalled SQL function declarations can register their bodies in the shared graph; a focused test covers this capability outside this optimized-view corpus.

PostgreSQL diagnostic printing now handles the parsed interval qualifier in FLOOR(timestamp TO unit) exactly as its validated symbol, without mutating the SQL tree. The failing original catalog runs are retained.
limitations: This transports catalog schemas reachable from optimized-view scans after compilation, not the complete ordered statement stream or catalog versions at each lowering boundary. Detached S1-to-S2 remains open.
JDBC tables, complete join system-field metadata and cross-arena aggregate/expression operator sharing remain open.
The catalog validates metadata and scan edges; the expression verifier validates contexts. Whole-program statement and correlation-scope ownership is still required.
The diagnostic fix has focused coverage and full successful catalog reconstruction; production before/after full-prefix comparison is a separate pending check.
Independent review and other P0 gates remain open.
